hero.title: GREEN HORIZON: YOUTH VOICES FOR CLIMATE ACTION THROUGH DRONE TECHNOLOGY
hero.subtitle: An Erasmus+ youth partnership equipping young people and youth workers with practical skills in camera drone piloting, environmental photography, and visual storytelling to document climate challenges and drive community action.

promo_video.heading: Our Project from Above
promo_video.subtitle: Experience our local environments and transnational field training through aerial camera perspectives captured by youth participants.
promo_video.title: Green Horizon: Official Promotional Video
promo_video.description: The official promotional film of Green Horizon captures transnational youth climate advocacy and aerial drone perspectives across Germany, Romania, and Türkiye. From urban parklands in Bonn and Carpathian mountain canopies in Brașov to Mediterranean coastlines in Mersin, young participants document environmental shifts, champion conscious consumption, and prove how digital aerial skills inspire local ecological change.

results_section.heading: What We Created Together
results_section.subtitle: Explore the three tangible results developed during the Green Horizon partnership.

result_1.title: Educational Booklet
result_1.description: Combines climate change mitigation principles, photographic composition masterclasses, camera drone flight safety, 6 flight drills, and a printable field checklist.

result_2.title: Short Climate Campaigns
result_2.meta: Documentary series · 3 videos from Germany, Romania and Türkiye
result_2.description: Grid of 3 documentary short films filmed and edited by youth participants, documenting riverbank health, forest recovery, and coastal ecosystems from above.

result_3.title: VR-Enhanced Photo Exhibition
result_3.description: Drone photos by young people from Germany, Romania and Türkiye. Presented at the dissemination conferences in July 2026 and online as a virtual exhibition since October 2026.

partnership_section.heading: Where We Worked
partnership_section.subtitle: Connecting youth across Germany, Romania, and Türkiye: Bonn (DE), Mersin (TR), and Brașov (RO).
